title: Finite Tor intervals and bounded flat models on a ringed site
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention], and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Use the abelian category of sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], its unbounded derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], and derived tensor computed by K-flat resolutions [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Let $K\in D(R)$ and $a\leq b$ be integers. The following conditions are equivalent:

(1) For every sheaf $M$ of $R$-modules placed in degree zero, $H^i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)=0$ whenever $i\notin[a,b]$.

(2) There is a cochain complex $P$ of $R$-module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], with every $P^i$ flat (tensoring with it is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]), $P^i=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$, and an isomorphism $K\simeq P$ in $D(R)$.

No constructibility hypothesis, existence of enough points, or constant-coefficient assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Install the existing sheafified symmetric monoidal structure, tensorPreadditive, the proved small internal-Hom closed structure exposed by nonempty_monoidalClosed_independentCoefficients, the canonical functorial flat resolution, and isGrothendieckAbelianOfUniverses. Transport exactness along siteSheafTensorRightIso and symmetry to identify IsFlatOnSite with categorical ObjectProperty.flat. No site universes are identified.

For a degree-zero test sheaf M, choose a cochain representative L of K and apply the proved generic CochainComplex.exists_quasiIso_flat_kFlat to obtain P -> L. Its categorical K-flatness implies the live acyclic-tensor predicate: tensor the quasi-isomorphism 0 -> Z for any acyclic Z, and use that tensor preserves zero objects. Apply wfSiteDerivedTensor_first from def-wf-tensor-product to P and M[0]. Compose with the generic QObjTensorQObjIsoOfKFlatLeft, the localization of P -> L, and singleFunctorIsoCompQ. This gives an isomorphism from wfSiteDerivedTensor(K,M[0]) to the generic derived monoidal tensor K tensor M[0]. Transport homology vanishing along it and use isGE_iff/isLE_iff to identify the stated condition with categorical torAmplitudeIn.

Apply the already proved generic DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn_iff_exists_iso_Q_obj_flat. Its reverse implication uses bounded flat K-flatness; its forward implication tests against the unit, takes a same-upper-bound flat resolution, proves the lower opcycles flat by the Tor criterion, and forms the good lower truncation. Thus the original flat-resolution and truncation argument is retained inside this generic tool. Convert its categorical flatness termwise to IsFlatOnSite, convert IsStrictlyGE/LE to zero terms outside the interval, and reverse the representing isomorphism. These conversions work in both directions, including the zero ring, empty site, and a=b.
